note: v1, SO FAR: THE WHOLE SHAPE STANDING (the song I wanted to make; 4:42, 130 BPM, F). THE IDEA: take a number; halve it if it is even, treble it and add one if it is odd; go on until you reach one. Every number anyone has tried gets there and nobody has proved every number must. The song tries the first sixteen, in order, and plays each walk in full, end to end; nothing is repeated or cut to fit. A NUMBER IS THREE THINGS: its length (n sixteenths); its note (the n-th harmonic of the low F: 3 is C, 5 A, 7 E-flat, 9 G, 11 B, 13 D-flat), so a halving falls an octave in half the time; and its riff (its odd part written in twos, a stroke for a one and a rest for a nought, said round and round: 40, 20, 10, 5 is one phrase in half notes, quarters, eighths, sixteenths). Every walk ends alike: sixteen, eight, four, two, one, a ball coming to rest on F. The kit is outside the rule and keeps common time throughout. LISTEN FOR: 0:17.4, seven (288 sixteenths, eighteen bars exactly), where the second guitar joins; 2:06.7-2:28.2, twelve and thirteen on the ondes and the bass alone over a ride and a rim; 2:28.2, fourteen: seven said at half speed, then seven's whole walk again; 3:03.0, fifteen, eighty seconds long: it climbs to 160 (ten bars on one chord at 3:43) and the ondes, which plays each number at its true height, is out of sight from 3:43 to 4:11 and comes back from the top at 40; 4:26.7, the wheel four, two, one (one is not an end), fifteen turns of seven sixteenths, which is what brings it back to a bar line. THE BAND: two ct-twin guitars, ct-bass, ct-kit, and the library ondes Martenot as the lead. THE DRAW'S ROUND TYPE WAS instrument; on an empty slot the first round is the song, and the one instrument I set by measurement is the lead: 2.5 dB off each note per octave over middle C (a sine stood 2.5 dB under the band up high and 8.8 down low), its diffuser halved and 3 dB off at 350 Hz (it held 45% of 250-500 Hz; now 24%). MEASURED (seeds 0/11): 87.033 / 85.134; the first bare draft read 79.62 / 80.192. Against the eleven records 250-500 Hz reads 2.5 to 2.9 dB over in the long walks (4.2 in the opening on one guitar); everything else within 2.4 dB except 8-16 kHz in the climb (+3.5). The loud walks all sit within 1 dB of each other (-12.0 to -13.2 K); twelve and thirteen are 4 dB under. No card: nothing here needs his ear to go on. WHICH OF HIS RULES I TOOK AS BINDING: all of direction.rules; no words, so the vocal rules do not arise. Not heard by me.
next: It is bare, and anyone may build on it. In order of what I would do: (1) DYNAMICS: the loud walks are one level and one texture (variety is the weak term, 64-70): give nine, eleven and fifteen each a different kit feel and guitar register; fifteen's climb (3:03-3:43) should grow, and 160 should be the biggest thing in the song. (2) The opening seventeen seconds (one to six) are one guitar and a kick at full level: a real entrance. (3) The ondes: whether out of sight should be silence (as now) or something else is an ear's call; TOP in the generator is the top of the ribbon, TILT its level slope, --lead-gain its fader. (4) The second guitar's small phrase under 40, 80 and 160 could be a different sound. (5) 250-500 Hz is still 2.5-2.9 over: the guitars hold 30% of it (the album's 380 Hz cut is not on them here). Do not cut or repeat a walk to make the form tidier: that each takes as long as it takes is the song. --form prints where each walk starts.

note:
v2, THE SUMMIT HAS ITS FALL INSIDE IT (chirper-three; section round, windows 8 and 9; the change is 3:43.2–4:10.9, the top of the fifteenth walk and its first step down). v1's note asked that 160 be the biggest thing in the song. Measured, it was the smallest of the loud stretches: ten bars on one chord, the left guitar striking twice and ringing for half of it, 1.9 dB under the long walks in the finished file. LISTEN FOR 3:43.2, the top: four guitars now, the new pair on the low A, a crash, the hands on the china; under the chord the bass no longer holds, it moves (A, a short F, A: a phrase two and a half bars long, said four times under the chord). 4:01.6, 80: the left guitar comes down to what the new pair is already playing. 4:10.9, 40: the new pair stops and the whole band is on the riff the bass has had since the top; the ondes comes back there as before.
THE IDEA: 160 is not one number. It is 80 doubled and 40 doubled twice, down to five: ONE phrase (stroke, rest, stroke) in six sizes, and from the top the walk does nothing but go down through them. v1 played two of the sizes at the top (the number's own, two bars a place, on the left guitar; the smallest, in sixteenths, on the right guitar and the kick). Now the sizes between are heard, each on what will have it next: TWO MORE GUITARS (the album's wall rig, new tracks wall-left and wall-right) say eighty's phrase, a bar a place, a storey under the number (A1, E2, A2); the BASS says forty's, half a bar a place, exactly as it plays it at 40. So at the top every chord of the next thirty seconds is already going, and the fall takes a storey off at a time. The kit's hands stay in common time, as v1 rules; the foot, which is in the rule, is lifted on the four of the new pair's six chords that it had played softly.
WHAT CHANGED: 18 notes on the two new tracks; the bass's six notes in 160 and 80 become eighteen; four kick strokes go from 0.78 to 0.95; the ride's 40 quarters in 160 are the china and one crash is added at 3:43.2. No walk is cut, repeated or moved, and no guitar, ondes or snare note changed.
WHAT I MEASURED (raw window on seed 0, then finished files on seeds 0 and 11). FIRST BENCH, not kept: the new pair at the album's setting (-3.5 dB, 3 dB off at 380 Hz) lifted 160 by 1.9 dB raw but put 3.3 dB into 250-500 Hz, where v1's note already reads the song 2.5 to 2.9 over the records. KEPT: the pair at -1 dB with 6 dB off at 380 Hz. Finished, 160 reads -13.89 -> -11.55 and -13.84 -> -11.63 dB (K; +2.3 and +2.2), and 80 reads -13.07 -> -11.52 and -11.50 (+1.6). THAT MAKES 160 LEVEL WITH THE LOUDEST STRETCH OF THE SONG, NOT OVER IT: the start of the fifteenth walk reads -11.54 and -11.64, the other long walks -12.0. It is the biggest by what is in it (four guitars, the low A, the china), and by half a decibel over seven, nine, eleven and fourteen. COST, benched raw at -2 dB on the pair (the kept setting is 1 dB up on that and was not benched for this): 160 carries 1.8 dB more of its level at 250-500 Hz than the walks either side (2.8 more in 80), and the china puts +4.5 dB at 8-16 kHz for those ten bars. Everything outside 3:43.2–4:10.9 is unchanged on both seeds (-66.5 dB residual or lower, 0.006 dB or less); the first half second of 40 differs by -44 dB (the pair's last chord ringing out). Loudness target -9.81 (was -10): at -10 every other bar came out 0.17 to 0.18 dB quieter.
SCORES 0/11: 87.033/85.134 -> 86.685/85.590 (-0.35, +0.46): kept on judgment. Variety rises on both seeds (70.4 -> 71.7, 64.6 -> 65.9). Structure falls on seed 0 (68.4 -> 65.3) and rises on seed 11 (64.0 -> 65.3): the scorer counts 21 sections where it wants at most 19, and on one of its seven cuts the count moved by one. -9.8 LUFS, -1.29 dBTP.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether four guitars on one chord for ten bars read as a summit or as a wall with the detail gone; whether the bass's moving line is heard under them; whether the low A1 chords are weight or mud.

No card. Not checked by ear.

next: STOREY in the generator is 'rig ; track gain ; pan ; octaves from the left guitar's chord ; dB at 380 Hz' for the second pair. If the top is mud, put the pair at the left guitar's own octave (field four = 0) before lowering it; if the pair buries the left guitar's two strokes, -3 in field two. Re-fit SUMMIT_LOUDNESS after any change (render once, read the gain of an untouched minute against v1, move the target by it). STILL TO DO, from v1's list: 160 is level with the loudest stretch, not over it, and the way to make it the biggest is to bring the CLIMB up to it (15 to 53, 3:03–3:43, does not grow: 106 and 53 read 1 dB UNDER the walk's first bars) and to give nine, eleven and fourteen their own levels, not to push the top into the limiter. The sizes not yet heard at the top are 20 and 10 (a quarter and an eighth a place): a second voice for them would finish the tower, and the ondes, which is out of sight there, is the obvious one if it may play below its true height. The kit's hands stay outside the rule (v1): do not put them on the phrase. 250-500 Hz is still over on the whole song: the first pair has no cut at 380 Hz. Do not cut or repeat a walk.

note:
v3, THE BASS GETS THE ALBUM'S CHAIN (instrument round: the bass; no note of the song changes). v1 and v2 had the bass on a bare track (a high-pass and one cut). I read the song against the album's eleven records and by part first. WHAT THE READ SAID (finished v2, the four long walks): 20-60 Hz 1.9 to 2.3 dB OVER, 60-120 Hz 1.5 to 2.0 SHORT, 250-500 Hz 2.5 to 2.9 over, 8-16 kHz 1.4 to 1.8 over; 500 Hz to 8 kHz within 0.8 (the guitars are right). By part (raw, the ninth walk): the bass sat 10.8 dB under the rest of the band (K) and its level moved 4.7 dB from note to note; under 120 Hz it is the kick and the bass, and the bass's weight was all on its fundamental.
WHAT CHANGED: the bass goes through the chain the album's bass has on tracks 1, 7, 8 and 14: its weight moved from the fundamental (a cut at 44 Hz) to the octave above (a lift at 90 Hz), the box out at 350 Hz, 4 dB of string at 1.5 kHz, a compressor at 8:1. Here the chain is on the bass's own track with the fader after it.
LISTEN FOR: any long walk (0:52 the ninth): the bass line under the two guitars should be easier to follow, and the low end firmer rather than deeper. 2:06.7-2:28.2, twelve and thirteen, where the bass and the ondes are alone: the bass's own tone, before and after, is plainest there.
MEASURED. The bass in the band (raw, K): 10.8 -> 9.0 dB under the rest in the ninth walk, its notes 4.7 -> 3.3 dB apart; at the top (160, four guitars) 12.2 -> 11.3 under, and its share of 60-120 Hz there -14.2 -> -9.7 dB; its share of 1-2 kHz in the ninth walk -17.4 -> -12.8 dB. THE MIX AGAINST THE RECORDS (seed 0; seed 11 within 0.3), the four long walks: 20-60 Hz +1.9..+2.3 -> +1.4..+1.7; 60-120 Hz -1.5..-2.0 -> -0.9..-1.2; 250-500 Hz +2.5..+2.9 -> +2.2..+2.6. COST: 120-250 Hz goes from level to 0.3 to 0.5 over. Every stretch of the finished file is within 0.11 dB (K) of v2.
THE QUIET WALKS, and a thing learned: v1 plays the bass 5 dB down in twelve and thirteen. The chain's compressor gave most of that back (the stretch came out 0.6 dB louder, a tenth of the song's one drop gone). A trim on the notes did nothing (1.5 dB off each note moved the stretch 0.02 dB: the compressor undoes it), so the trim (1.5 dB) is on the fader, after the chain, for those two walks only: the stretch reads -15.5 (v2 -15.3) and the bass stands where it stood against the ondes (0.9 under), with its new tone.
SCORES 0/11: 87.587 / 86.291 (v2 86.685 / 85.590). -9.8 LUFS, -1.29 dBTP. --without-low-bus gives v2 byte for byte; --without-storeys still gives v1.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEND (for the next instrument rounds, with numbers): the KICK is 78% of 20-60 Hz and its body peaks at 53 Hz, just under the records' weight: that band is still 1.4 to 1.7 over and 60-120 still about 1 short. The CYMBALS: 8-16 kHz 1.2 to 1.5 over (3.2 in the climb), and the scorer's worst band is 14.8 kHz, 10 dB over: the kit here has neither the album's shelf over 9 kHz nor its low-pass at 14.25 kHz. 250-500 Hz: the guitars hold about half of it, the snare a quarter, the kick a fifth.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether the bass now sounds like a bass guitar with weight or like one with its bottom taken out; whether more of it under the guitars is wanted. Not heard by me. No card.

INSTRUMENTS STILL TO DO, each with its number: (1) THE KICK: 78% of 20-60 Hz, body at 53 Hz; that band reads 1.4 to 1.7 over the records and 60-120 Hz about 1 short. Move its weight up (the album's kit carries a lift near 92 Hz on The Other Hand's drums bus; or retune the drum in a song-local kit). (2) THE CYMBALS: 8-16 kHz 1.2 to 1.5 over, 3.2 in the climb; the scorer's worst band is 14.8 kHz, 10 dB over. If the bass now sounds thin, raise the 44 Hz band from -7 toward -4 in BASS before going back to v2; if it is too forward, the fader (0 dB). note: v4, THE KIT (instrument round: the kick, the cymbals and the drums bus; no note of the song changes). LISTEN FOR any long walk (0:52, the ninth): the kick is a shade higher and not as heavy-handed, the low end steadier under the bass chirper-alpha set in v3; the cymbals have lost a little glare. 3:03-3:43, the climb, where the china is busiest, is where the top changes most. WHAT THE READ SAID OF v3 (the kit alone against the eleven records' drum stems, as a share of the mix, and the mix against their mixes; raw, the ninth walk and the climb): the kit as a whole stood 1.3 and 1.8 dB over the records' drums. THE KICK alone was 44 and 50% of the whole mix's power, 77 and 88% of everything under 60 Hz, with its drum on the low A (55 Hz), so nearly all its weight was under 60, where the song read 1.4 to 1.7 over. THE CYMBALS were 95% and more of 8-16 kHz (1.2 to 1.5 over, 3.2 in the climb). The kit held 6.6 dB more of 250-500 Hz than the records' drums. WHAT CHANGED. (1) The kick's drum is tuned a semitone up, to B flat (58 Hz, the fourth of the key): its body now straddles 60 Hz as the records' kicks do (60-120 against 20-60 Hz: -0.5 -> +2.8 dB), and its fader comes down 1.5 dB (2 -> 0.5). (2) The cymbals' track gets the album's shelf, 2 dB off over 9 kHz. (3) The drums bus gets the album's top (2 dB off over 9 kHz, low-pass at 14.25 kHz where it had 14.8) and a narrow, deeper cut for the box, 7 dB at 340 Hz q 1.2 (was 4 at 390): narrow because the song is SHORT at 500 Hz-1 kHz, so the album's wide cut at 400 would have taken from the wrong place too. MEASURED, THE MIX, finished, the four long walks against the records (seed 0; seed 11 within 0.2): 20-60 Hz +1.4..+1.7 -> +0.4..+0.8; 60-120 Hz -0.9..-1.2 -> -0.4..-0.7; 8-16 kHz +1.2..+1.5 -> -0.1..+0.4; 250-500 Hz +2.2..+2.6 -> +1.8..+2.3; 500 Hz-8 kHz within 0.7 as before. The climb at 8-16 kHz +3.2 -> +1.9. THE KIT ALONE against the records' drums: whole +1.3/+1.8 -> +0.8/+1.3; under 60 Hz +1.7/+2.2 -> +0.2/+0.8; 250-500 Hz +6.6 -> +4.2. The kick is 37 and 43% of the mix (was 44 and 50) and stands 3.7 and 2.7 dB under everything else (K; was 2.6 and 1.7). COST: the top (160, 3:43) and the last walk were not over at 8-16 kHz and are now 0.8 and 2.2 under (were +0.2 and -0.9); every stretch of the finished file is 0.08 to 0.13 dB quieter (K), the two quiet walks unchanged. SCORES, seeds 0/11: 87.834 / 87.991 (v3 87.587 / 86.291); spectrum 89.6 -> 94.9 on both. -9.8 LUFS, -1.29 dBTP. TRIED AND NOT KEPT, with numbers: the kick on C (65 Hz): the mix went from 1.6 over to 2.6 UNDER below 60 Hz, the read's edge at 60 Hz being just where a kick's body sits; 3 dB off the cymbals over 9 kHz: the long walks 0.6 to 1.3 under at 8-16 kHz (it scored highest, 88.125 / 88.411: the scorer likes less top than the records have); 1 dB off the cymbals' fader as well as the shelf: 0.2 to 0.8 under, and the top and last walk lost most. WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether the kick still hits as hard as the riff wants (it is the riff's foot, 1.5 dB lower now), or whether B flat under an F riff is heard as a pitch at all. No card. --without-kit gives v3 byte for byte; --without-low-bus and --without-storeys give what they gave. Not heard by me.
next: THE KIT is read and set (KIT in the generator: the kick's pitch ; its fader ; the cymbals' fader ; their eq ; the drums bus's eq ; the loudness target). If the kick is now too polite, give back the fader first ('kick gain': 1.25), not the tuning; if B flat is heard as a note against the riff, A#1 -> A1 and take 2 dB off the kick under 60 Hz another way. STILL OPEN ON THE READ: 250-500 Hz, 1.8 to 2.3 over in the long walks: the kit is no longer most of it (the kick holds 9 to 16% there now): it is the first pair of guitars, which have no cut at 380 Hz (the album's walls carry 3 dB there; try 2 on left and right and read 500 Hz-1 kHz, which must not fall). THE SNARE has not been touched: against the records' drums the kit is still 7.4 dB over at 500 Hz-1 kHz and 3.8 over at 1-2 kHz, and that is the snare's body and crack; but the MIX is 0 to 0.7 short there, so it is right as it is unless the guitars come up in that band. THE CLIMB (3:03-3:43) is still 1.9 over at 8-16 kHz and the top and last walk 0.8 and 2.2 under: that is the writing (the china through the climb), not the kit's tone: a ride or a closed hat for the first half of the climb would mend it and help the climb GROW, which v2's list asks for (15 to 53 does not grow; nine, eleven and fourteen want their own levels; 20 and 10 not yet heard at the top). v5, THE BAND IS AS BIG AS THE NUMBER (whole song; no note changes). A number here was three things: its length, its note, its riff. It had no SIZE. Every loud walk was one level from its first number to its last (all within a decibel; the scorer's variety 62 to 72), so 160 was no bigger than 13 and a walk reached one at the level it had left 52. v1 asked that the climb grow and that 160 be the biggest thing in the song; v2 measured that the climb did not grow. Now it follows from the rule and nothing is set by hand: THE GUITARS' AND THE BASS'S FADERS STAND 1.25 dB HIGHER FOR EVERY DOUBLING OF THE NUMBER BEING SAID (as they were at 32; from -6.25 dB at one to +2.9 at 160). A halving is a step down; a trebling is a step and a half up.
LISTEN FOR: 0:00-0:17, the song opens small: one to six are small numbers, and it grows into seven. 0:41.5-0:50.7, the end of the seventh walk: 40, 20, 10, 5, then 16, 8, 4, 2, 1, each a step smaller and sooner: a ball coming to rest (every walk ends this way). 3:03-3:43, fifteen's climb: 46, 23, 70, 35, 106, 53: up, half back, up further. 3:43.2, 160: the biggest thing in the song, because it is the biggest number in it. 4:26.7, the wheel four, two, one turning small under the hands, and at 4:38.8 the last bar line at full size.
THE FOOT AND THE HANDS: the kick plays the riff's strokes, so it is in the rule and settles with the walk (it never goes over its v4 level: its lane is capped there). The snare and cymbals are outside the rule, as v1 has it, and keep one level: common time goes on while the walk settles.
MEASURED (finished files, seeds 0/11, K): the opening -10.3 -> -11.2; the four long walks -9.7 -> -9.8 (their average is held: the reference 32 was chosen so the guitars' power over the song is what it was, which keeps the kit v4 set against them in its place); the quiet walks -15.5 -> -15.7; the climb 15 to 53 -9.7 -> -9.0; 160 -9.3 -> -8.3; 80 -9.2 -> -8.6; the wheel -8.6 -> -10.5; the last chord -8.3 -> -8.0. So 160 stands 1.5 dB over the long walks (0.4 in v4) and the song's loud stretches span 3 dB where they spanned 1. Alone (raw), at the end of the seventh walk the guitars and bass read -1.3, -2.5, -3.8, -5.0, -6.1 dB on 16, 8, 4, 2, 1 against v4, exactly the lane; the kick -0.9, -2.0, -2.9, -3.8, -4.7 (its bus's compressor gives a quarter back).
WHAT IT DOES NOT DO, measured: inside a walk the whole mix moves only 0.33 dB for each dB on the faders, because the hands hold their level and count for most of the mix's loudness; and a big number's phrase is sparse (52 is said in quarter notes), so 52 is still the quietest cell of the seventh walk in the finished file (-11.3 -> -10.5; its neighbours -10.1). The size is in the guitars, not yet in the whole band. AT THE TOP the limiter works harder: in 160 the crest falls 11.0 -> 10.1 dB and 0.16% of samples stand within half a decibel of the ceiling (0.08% before).
SCORES 0/11: 90.248 / 92.046 (v4 87.834 / 87.991): variety 70.6 / 71.4 -> 83.6 / 86.3, structure 67.5 -> 69.6 / 75.8. -9.8 LUFS, -1.29 dBTP. --without-size gives v4 byte for byte; --without-kit, --without-low-bus and --without-storeys still give v3, v2 and v1. SIZE in the generator is 'dB for each doubling ; the number at which the band is as loud as it was ; the last chord's size'.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether a band that swells and settles with its numbers is heard as the walk's shape or as someone riding the faders; whether the walk-ends now sound like a ball coming to rest or like the guitars dropping out under a loud kit. Not heard by me. No card.

The point stands as said in the note: a big number's phrase is sparse, so in the whole mix the biggest numbers of a walk are not yet its loudest cells; the cure is in the notes.

v6, THE GUITARS GET THEIR BODY (chirper-three; instrument round: the first pair of guitars; no note of the song changes). The bass had its round (v3) and the kit (v4); the two guitars had never been read. LISTEN FOR any long walk (0:52, the ninth): the muted low-string strokes between the chords should have more weight of their own, at the sides where the guitars are, where it used to be the bass's in the middle. 3:03-3:43, the climb, is where the guitars are loudest and the change is largest.
WHAT THE READ SAID OF v5 (raw, seed 0; the ninth walk and the climb to 160). THE PAIR ALONE against the records' guitar heard alone (tools/cabspec.py: obZen 3:03, Combustion 0:44, Bleed 6:27): 141-282 Hz 6.3 and 4.9 dB SHORT; 400 to 800 Hz 5.4 to 7.2 over; mean distance 2.80 and 2.67 dB. THE PAIR IN THE MIX against the eleven records' guitar stems, as a share of the mix: 120-250 Hz 5.3 and 3.1 dB SHORT; 500 Hz-1 kHz 4.2 and 4.9 over; every other band from 60 Hz to 8 kHz within 1.9. Two yardsticks, the same shape. THE MIX DID NOT SHOW IT (120-250 Hz reads +0.4 against the records' mixes) because others held the band for the guitars: in the ninth walk the kick has 37% of the mix's 120-250 Hz, the bass 35%, the two guitars 16%. On the records the guitars stand 4.8 dB OVER the bass there; here they stood 3.4 under it, and the bass was 2.9 dB over the records' basses. A low-tuned guitar's weight is in that band (the low F's third to fifth harmonics: 131, 175 and 218 Hz), and this rig cuts it before the amp: the library patch's 'tight' filter is at 220 Hz.
WHAT CHANGED. (1) The pair's tight filter comes down to 180 Hz: more of the low string reaches the amp. (2) The bass gives the band up: the last cut of its chain, at 170 Hz, goes from 3 dB to 5. (3) In the two quiet walks (2:06.7-2:28.2) there are no guitars to give it to, and the deeper cut took 0.66 dB off the bass alone there, so its fader trim in those walks goes from -1.5 to -0.85 dB.
MEASURED, THE PARTS (raw, seed 0, ninth walk and climb). The pair against the records' guitars at 120-250 Hz: -5.3 -> -3.0 and -3.1 -> -0.3. The bass against the records' basses there: +2.9 -> +1.4 in both. Share of the mix's 120-250 Hz: the pair 16 -> 27% and 27 -> 45%; the bass 35 -> 24% and 35 -> 21%: the guitars now hold more of it than the bass, as on the records. The pair alone against the records' guitar alone: 141-282 Hz -6.3 -> -4.7 and -4.9 -> -3.3; mean distance 2.80 -> 2.53 and 2.67 -> 2.50. So it is LESS THAN HALF THE WAY in the ninth walk (2.3 dB of 5.3) and nearly all of it in the climb.
MEASURED, THE MIX (finished files, seeds 0 and 11, against the eleven mixes). 120-250 Hz in the four long walks: within 0.1 dB of v5 (0.0 to +0.5): the band changed hands and kept its level. THE COSTS: in the climb that band goes +0.6 -> +1.2 and +0.7 -> +1.1 (the guitars' faders are highest there); 250-500 Hz, where the long walks were already 2.0 to 2.6 over, is up to 0.2 dB more; the bass stands 0.7 dB further under everything else (read raw on seed 0, K: -9.0 -> -9.6 in the ninth walk, -8.3 -> -9.1 in the climb), which is 0.7 of the 1.8 dB v3 gained for it; the opening (one guitar) is 0.11 to 0.15 dB quieter. BENCHED AND NOT KEPT, with numbers (the pair alone, ninth walk, unless said). The amp's own knobs: mid 0.74 -> 0.35 took 1.2 to 1.5 dB off 630-800 Hz; bass 0.5 -> 0.8, resonance 0.72 -> 1 and the microphone at 0.03 moved 141-282 Hz by 0.4, 0.0 and 0.2 dB. An eq lift of 4 dB at 200 Hz: it put 1.3 dB into the pair's 250-500 Hz. Tight at 150 Hz without the bass's cut: the mix's 120-250 Hz went to +1.3. THE ALBUM'S GUITAR BUS (2 dB off at 330 Hz and a room of 0.35 s at 6%): with it the pair read 1.3 UNDER the records' guitars at 250-500 Hz in the ninth walk, and the room filled the riff's rests, which are this song's noughts: the quietest tenth of the pair's 10 ms frames rose from 60 dB under the loud ones to 28 under. A SCOOP of 2 dB at 600 Hz: the mix went 0.5 and 0.7 dB further under at 500 Hz-1 kHz, where the climb is already short. HARD LEFT AND RIGHT: the pair as panned reads 0.20 left against right in every band; the records' guitar stems read 0.00 (their widest 0.18); the two guitars alone are 0.00 against each other, so they are two players already, and going from 0.9 to 1 cost the pair 0.7 dB in the mix's read.
WHAT ELSE THE READ FOUND, for whoever is next. 250-500 Hz in the long walks is NOT the guitars' (v4's note thought so): in the ninth walk the ondes holds 39% of it, the snare 23%, the two guitars 29%, the kick 8%, the bass 4%, and the guitars are not over the records' guitars there (+0.3, +1.3 in the climb). It is the lead's own notes when the number is seven to eleven (311-494 Hz); without its halo the ondes still holds 36%.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether the low string still stops cleanly with more of it in the amp (the rests read as silent as before, but that is not the same thing); whether the bass, 0.7 dB further under, is as easy to follow as v3 left it; whether the weight is heard as the guitars' or only as low-mid moved outwards.

note:
v7, THE NUMBERS ARE AT THEIR TRUE HEIGHT (whole song; 986 notes repitched, by up to 49 cents; none added, dropped, moved or changed in length or level). LISTEN FOR 0:17.4, the seventh walk: 7, 22, 11, 34, 17, 52, 26, 13. Each chord and each note of the ondes is now an overtone of the low string the band is chugging on; the sevens, elevens and thirteens are no longer the piano's notes. Then 2:14.4, thirteen on the ondes and the bass alone, where it is plainest. Not checked by ear, and this is a round an ear must judge: one card (below).
THE DRAW WAS A PALETTE ROUND. I took the song's whole palette of pitches and not one instrument: it is a choice, so I say so. The engine feature is new to the album (pitches as fractional key numbers).
WHY. The rule: "a number is the n-th harmonic of the low F", and the ondes "IS the number, at its true height". Until now every pitch was the semitone NEAREST the harmonic. That is 31 cents off for 7, 14 and 28; 49 off for 11 and 22; 41 for 13, 26 and 52; 45 for 35 and 70; 28 for 23 and 46; 27 for 53 and 106; 14 for 5 and all its doublings up to 160. Now every pitched note is the harmonic itself: the ondes at n times the low F exactly; the guitars' chord, the second pair's and the bass on the same harmonic brought down by octaves, with a pure fifth. The muted low-string strokes are the fundamental, as they were.
WHAT IT DOES TO THE WALK, and it is in v1's own words: "trebled-and-one it leaps up a twelfth AND A HAIR". In semitones the hair was a whole semitone or nothing, by the luck of the rounding (7 -> 22 a semitone, 11 -> 34 nothing, 13 -> 40 a semitone, 17 -> 52 nothing). True, it is one part in 3n: a tone at 3 -> 10, a semitone at 5 -> 16, then 80 cents at 7 -> 22, 63 at 9 -> 28, 52 at 11 -> 34, 44 at 13 -> 40, 38 at 15 -> 46, 34 at 17 -> 52, 25 at 23 -> 70, 16 at 35 -> 106, 11 at 53 -> 160. The bigger the number, the finer the hair; and a halving is a pure octave every time. The size of a number can be heard in the size of its step.
MEASURED (the pitched band alone, raw, seed 0). The ondes's line against the harmonic, for 10, 11, 13, 14 and 15: +13.7, +49.2, -40.9, +31.3, +11.8 cents before; 0.0, -0.3, -0.2, -0.1, 0.0 after. Finished file: every walk's level is within 0.10 dB (K) of v6's; -9.9 LUFS as before; the loudness target is not moved. What I looked for and did not find: a drop in roughness round the ondes's note (the level's wobble at 3 to 40 Hz there: 21.8% before, 20.0% after, over twenty numbers): the retuning is exact, but I cannot show by a meter that it sounds smoother.
SCORES 0/11: 90.435 / 91.235 (v6 90.875 / 91.884): half a point down, kept on judgment. It is the scorer's variety term (86.8 -> 82.1, 85.7 -> 81.1): with the pitches moved it cuts the song one section differently at one of its settings, and reads a smaller spread of levels between the sections it finds (5.4 -> 4.7 dB) although the walks' own levels did not move.
WHAT I CANNOT KNOW, and it is the whole question: whether a power chord 49 cents under B over a low F reads as the string's own eleventh overtone or as a wrong note. On one fundamental the series is consonant in the way an alphorn or a throat singer is; to an ear set by the other sixteen songs it may only sound flat. --equal gives v6 back byte for byte.

WHAT TRUE HEIGHTS OPEN, not done: (1) the ondes has the library's vibrato (18 cents): a steadier ribbon (synth.pitch.mod.0.amount about 0.02) would let the finer hairs (16 cents at 35 -> 106, 11 at 53 -> 160, both out of the ondes's sight now) be heard on the guitars instead: they are there in the chords. (2) OUT OF SIGHT: above the ribbon's top (70, 106, 160, 80) the ondes rests; a true harmonic that high is a pure tone over the band, and one quiet sine at 160 times the low F (6985 Hz) would be the number itself at the summit. v1 left that to an ear. (3) The guitar string plays 3 to 7 cents sharp, more the higher (bead bd-d2ee40): not trimmed here (the roots are low, where it is least).

note: v8, THE HANDS REMEMBER (whole song, from the seventh walk on; only the snare changes and a closed hat is added: no guitar, bass, ondes, kick or cymbal note is touched, and no pitch). WHY: the walks merge. Seven's walk (7 22 11 34 17 52 26 13 40 20 10 5 16 8 4 2 1) is the whole of nine's after three numbers, of fourteen's after one, and eleven's is its last fifteen: between 0:58 and 3:03 the song says that one thirty-second passage three more times, and from 1:37 to 3:03 the only number it has not said before is twelve. Then the fifteenth walk's first nine numbers, 68 seconds, are all new. The band is in the rule and plays a number the same way every time; the hands are not, and v1 gave each walk one feel by hand (the scorer's structure term read 72 and 78). NOW THE HANDS KNOW WHERE THEY HAVE BEEN: what they play under a number depends on how many walks have said it before. Never said: half time, the snare on three alone. Said once: the backbeat. Said twice: the backbeat, and a closed hat on the off-beat eighths. Three times or more: double time, the snare on every off-beat (each stroke 2.5 dB lighter). A power of two (16 8 4 2 1), however often said: the backbeat, so every walk still comes to rest the same way. They never leave common time: every stroke is on a beat or half way between two. The two quiet walks keep their stick on the rim; walks one to six and the wheel are as they were. LISTEN FOR, in order: 0:17.4 seven found in half time, and at 0:45.3 (10, then 5) the hands recognise the way home for two seconds. 0:52.4 nine: 9, 28, 14 in half time, and at 0:58.3, on 7, the backbeat comes in: we have been here. 1:36.8 eleven, the third telling: the hat ticks between the cymbal's quarters. 2:28.2 fourteen: backbeat, hat, and from 2:33.1 (11) DOUBLE TIME to 2:59.4: the passage is fastest when it is best known. 3:03.0 fifteen: 67.8 seconds no walk has trodden, in HALF TIME (it had the backbeat), climbing to 160 and its china; at 4:10.8, on 40, said by five walks before, double time for 8.7 seconds, then the backbeat for the last sixteen, eight, four, two, one. Every walk from nine on ends 10, 5 in double time (1.7 s) before the ball comes to rest: the same small flourish each time. COUNTED: snare 234 strokes -> 265 (119 out, 150 in; 88 on off-beats); 62 hat strokes. MEASURED (raw benches): the hat in the eleventh walk stands 20.8 dB (K) under everything else and is 18% of 8-16 kHz (at 10 dB on its fader it stood 25.8 under: not a part anyone would hear; it is at 15). The double-time snare in the fourteenth walk stands 8.7 dB under everything else where v7's half-time snare stood 12.0; at the backbeat's own weight it stood 6.6 under and held 46% of 250-500 Hz, so its strokes are trimmed 2.5 dB. AGAINST THE ELEVEN RECORDS (finished, seed 0), the cost is at the top: 8-16 kHz in eleven +0.8 -> +1.7, in fourteen +0.8 -> +1.8 (and 250-500 Hz +2.6 -> +2.9), 40 to 1 -0.6 -> +0.1; the climb in half time reads 0.3 over at 250-500 where it read 0.6; nine and the top are as they were. UNTOUCHED BARS: one to six, seven's new ground, the two quiet walks and the last chord match v7 with residual -64 dB or lower; their gain is 0.009 dB under v7's on seed 0 and 0.024 on seed 11 with the loudness target at -9.826 (v7 -9.839; left there). SCORES 0/11: 90.828 / 93.415 (v7 90.435 / 91.235); structure 71.8 -> 74.9 and 78.0 -> 87.6, spectrum 93.3 -> 92.6 and 93.5 -> 92.8 (the top, above). -9.9 LUFS, -1.29 dBTP. --without-memory gives v7 byte for byte; the six older switches give what they gave. THE WAITING CARD sf-true-heights (chirper-two's, on the tuning) is not touched by this: no pitch moves, and its two passages (0:17.4, 2:14.4) keep their notes; the first now has a different snare from 0:45.3 only. WHAT I CANNOT KNOW: whether 68 seconds of half time under the climb is weight or drag (it had the backbeat's drive); whether double time under fourteen is the lift before the climb or a different song for half a minute; whether the 10, 5 flourish, six times, charms or grates. No card. Not heard by me.
